topics.title: AI safety warnings heat up
topics.summary: AI leaders and researchers renewed calls for stronger safeguards, while U.S. officials pushed back on slowing development amid competition with China.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone agrees the new tool is powerful but not everyone agrees on brakes, who in the studio gets to hold the instruction manual?

topics.title: EPA drops power-plant climate rule
topics.summary: The EPA moved to repeal greenhouse-gas limits for coal and natural-gas power plants, setting up a major legal and environmental fight.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a rule disappears and everyone claims the future is safer their way, who asks about the electric bill first?

topics.title: Saudi pipeline damage lifts oil worries
topics.summary: A damaged Saudi pipeline is expected to stay partly offline for weeks, raising concern about oil flows, shipping routes, and fuel prices.
topics.discussionPrompt: If one pipeline problem can ripple into everyone’s week, who starts conserving gas and who starts explaining geopolitics badly?

topics.title: Ukraine energy-strike claim disputed
topics.summary: Trump said Ukraine and Russia agreed not to hit energy targets, but Ukrainian officials sounded cautious and asked for guarantees.
topics.discussionPrompt: When someone announces a deal before everyone else sounds convinced, who claps politely and who starts checking the fine print?

topics.title: Sweden vote stays tight
topics.summary: Sweden’s centre-left opposition held a narrow lead as most votes were counted, leaving coalition talks likely to be complicated.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a whole country ends up in group-project mode after an election, who becomes the negotiator and who just brings coffee?

topics.title: UK donation fight grows
topics.summary: Reform UK faced new questions after Nigel Farage suggested large donations may run into problems under proposed election-law changes.
topics.discussionPrompt: When campaign money comes with footnotes, who wants a spreadsheet and who says every party needs better labels?

topics.title: Court blocks mail-tracking plan
topics.summary: A federal judge blocked parts of a plan involving Postal Service tracking of mail and election ballots, citing limits on agency authority.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the mail suddenly becomes an election argument, who trusts the system and who starts labeling every envelope dramatically?

topics.title: Floods and erosion test communities
topics.summary: Severe flooding in eastern India and hurricane damage along California’s Orange County coast put local emergency planning back in focus.
topics.discussionPrompt: When weather rewrites the plan, who checks on neighbors first and who tries to engineer the perfect backup plan?

topics.title: Alaska deep-sea sponges discovered
topics.summary: Scientists reported nine new sponge species from Alaska’s deep sea, while warning their habitat could face pressure from trawling and mining.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the ocean keeps introducing new roommates, who is amazed and who asks whether they pay rent?

topics.title: Kennedy Center finances wobble
topics.summary: Reports said Washington’s Kennedy Center faces serious financial strain, with leaders considering dramatic moves to avoid a possible closure.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an iconic venue says the budget is suddenly the main character, who proposes a fundraiser and who wants to inspect the books?
